rules.statement: Alerts are events with security implications and must be handled by the main processor or escalated to other hardware modules for action.

rules.condition: A peripheral defines an alert signal
rules.statement: Peripherals defining alerts must instantiate a prim_alert_sender to convert the alert event into a signal to the alert handler.
The differential signaling submodules may use either a synchronous or an asynchronous clocking scheme.
Alerts are differentially encoded and signaled with a full handshake on alert_p/n and ack_p/n, repeated as long as the alert is true.
The full handshake must back-pressure alert messages correctly so no alert is lost at the asynchronous boundary regardless of clock ratio.

rules.condition: Alert event is still true within the peripheral
rules.statement: The native alert message is repeated on the output wires as long as the alert event remains true.
The sender waits 2 cycles between handshakes.

rules.condition: Initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n received and synchronized, even if handshake lines are manipulated to emulate backpressure
rules.statement: The receiver must immediately propagate the first alert occurrence to alert_o after synchronizing the initial level change on alert_tx_i.alert_p/n.
The alert sender and receiver modules can be used either synchronously or asynchronously.
The signaling protocol remains the same in both synchronous and asynchronous use; synchronizer flops at the diff pair inputs may be omitted.

rules.condition: alert_tx_i.alert_p/n pair is not correctly encoded at the receiver
rules.statement: The receiver must assert integ_fail_o when alert_tx_i.alert_p/n is incorrectly encoded.

rules.condition: ping_p/n or ack_p/n pair is not correctly encoded at the sender
rules.statement: The sender must set alert_tx_o.alert_p/n to the same continuously toggling value, causing the receiver to assert integ_fail_o.

rules.condition: Signal integrity failures occur during ping or alert handshaking and the protocol locks up
rules.statement: A protocol lock-up must always trigger either a signal integrity alert or eventually a pingfail alert.
